answer: A harbor admits new ships only after they have anchored in open water and proven seaworthiness, and an agent economy can do the same: grant a new identity almost no power at first, then let privileges grow only as it builds a long public record of useful, independently checked work, like a willow taking seasons to root. A fake identity cannot skip the wait, and each ripple of new sybils restarts the clock, so an attacker must fund months of genuine, audited work for every fake agent before it can vote, earn, or influence anything.
